newsitem.title: USA: Fire damages historic black church in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Fire damages historic black church in Texas.

text.p: A fire Friday raged through an abandoned black church where the late Congresswoman Barbara Jordan was baptised and learned her powerful oratorical skills.
Houston Fire Department spokesman Rick Flanagan said the cause of the blaze was under investigation.
People living near the old Good Hope Missionary Baptist church said they heard explosions coming from the building, but Flanagan said it was not clear if the fire was accidental or a case of arson.
Flanagan said the old building suffered extensive damages and its fate was not certain. A fireman was injured when one of the walls fell over on a fire truck, but he was in good condition.

Work had been under way to restore the church, located in an area known as Freedmen's Town Historical District because it was once settled by freed slaves, and make it a community centre named for Jordan, who died in January 1996 from leukaemia at the age of 59.
Jordan was baptised at the church and worshipped there until the congregation moved into a new building a few miles away.

Jordan served in the U.S. House of Representatives from 1972 to 1979 and rose to national prominence in 1974 as a member of the House Judiciary Committee that voted to impeach President Richard Nixon for his role in the 1972 Watergate break-in and coverup. Her thundering speeches defending the Constitution made her one of the most recognised voices in public life.
Jordan said she had learned her oratorical skills partly from the Baptist preachers whose rousing sermons she listened to each Sunday while growing up in Houston.
